advances: An actual two-fiber fixed-cap local maximum with equal noncritical global budgets. It neither varies the cap thresholds nor asserts stability under arbitrary convex-body perturbations or at the actual critical depth budget.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
At either base each coordinate sees one low threshold $1/10$ and one high threshold $4/5$. The low-threshold triple covers the entire barycentric plane because $\sum_i\xi_i=1$. For each of the six ambient caps, the two traces give total area $V[(9/10)^2+(1/5)^2]=17V/20$. Bases $0,1$ are exposed and have no other integer bases between them; the convex hull of any nearby pair of triangles therefore has exactly those two sampled fibers.

Use the variance theorem at each triangle with $d=2$, the two fixed thresholds, and multipliers $5/11$. The normalized weight sum is $17/44$ at each vertex, the probability-weighted mean of $X$ is $22/17$, and the variance is $196/289$. Thus the physical blocks are stationary and the joint Hessian is their direct sum times $V$. In the order $(A_{01},A_{02},A_{10},A_{12},A_{20},A_{21})$, substitute these values into the normalized Hessian formula and use $b_j=-\sum_{i\ne j}A_{ij}$. The resulting matrix, multiplied by $-22$, is
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
13&5&0&0&0&-4\\
5&13&0&-4&0&0\\
0&0&13&5&-4&0\\
0&-4&5&13&0&0\\
0&0&-4&0&13&5\\
-4&0&0&0&5&13
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
Its diagonal is $13$ and each row has absolute off-diagonal sum $9$, so the matrix is positive definite by $2|ab|\le a^2+b^2$. For the characteristic polynomial of the normalized Hessian, write the matrix above as $13I+5P-4R$ where the transposition pairs of $P$ and $R$ are the positions of the $5$ and $-4$ entries. The pairs are the two alternating matchings on a six-cycle. Ordering the odd and even cycle vertices separately makes the off-diagonal block $5I-4S$ for a three-cycle permutation $S$. Its squared singular values are the eigenvalues of $41I-20(S+S^{\mathsf T})$, namely $1,61,61$. The eigenvalues of the displayed matrix are therefore $13\pm1$ (once each) and $13\pm\sqrt{61}$ (twice each). Scaling by $-1/22$ gives the stated polynomial. At each sufficiently near non-reference pair the stationary Lagrangian is strictly less than at the reference by negative definiteness. Feasibility and positive multipliers make the total volume at most its reference value plus this strictly negative difference.

At either sampled base, a mixed containing cap costs at least the own-fiber ordinary depth. Conversely any own-fiber containing cap extends to a cap with that trace at its base and empty trace on the other compact fiber by choosing a sufficiently large finite base tilt of the appropriate sign. Thus depth on each base equals its own-fiber depth. Fact 03bc771bddd39a8a applies to the triangle, so its maximum is $(2/3)^2V=4V/9$. Dividing by $2V$ gives the two stated ratios.
statement:
Let $T$ be a $2$-simplex of area $V>0$ with barycentric functions $\xi_i$, $i=0,1,2$. The actual source $[0,1]\times T$ has two positive integer fibers. Fix the six ambient caps
$$H_i^L=\{\xi_i\ge 1/10+(7/10)z\},\qquad H_i^H=\{\xi_i\ge 4/5-(7/10)z\}.$$
They cover the source on the integer bases and each has mass $17V/20$. In the chart independently varying both physical labeled triangles and keeping these caps fixed, the original pair is a strict local total-volume maximum under the six cap inequalities at that common budget. With all six multipliers $5/11$, the normalized Lagrangian Hessian in either physical block has characteristic polynomial
$$\frac{(11x+6)(11x+7)(121x^2+143x+27)^2}{1771561}.$$
The actual maximum raw mixed depth of the reference source is $4V/9$, or $2/9$ of total mass, whereas the common cover budget is $17/40$ of total mass.
title: A strict physical simplex maximum under six equal global cap budgets
